supportStates.priority: At a common timestamp finish an otherwise legal support-transfer/door operation first only if all its actual prerequisites remain available through completion. Then resolve resource expiry and unmet control requirements, then ordinary Falling deadlines. A transfer cannot finish after its supporting hull or required mechanism has already been destroyed. No later Action retroactively avoids an impact.
supportStates.grounded: Actual full legal supporting footprint holds the vessel. Engine may be off. Engine activation and takeoff require fuel, intact hull, trained distinct operators and one coordinated6second pilot/engineer event outside initiative; it is the one vessel event for that round and includes only the stated takeoff, not extra travel.
supportStates.powered: Fuel>0 and hull>0 are necessary. While in initiative, both operators must contribute to the one coordinated event each numbered round. The previously established powered hold lasts to that round end; if either contribution is still missing then, support ends and ordinary Falling begins at that actual boundary. Fuel0 or hull0 removes powered lift immediately. Contributions already paid are not erased merely because the actor becomes unable afterward, but a later round requires new actual contributions. Outside initiative, interrupted sustained crew work enters initiative/actual six-second intervals without granting a new free period.
supportStates.moored: At the marked berth, both operators spend their coordinated event attaching the one cleat assembly. Outside initiative they work concurrently for6seconds. Once completed, actual intact lattice/cleat support bears the entire craft; choose engine-off or powered idle. No continuing crew Actions are required merely to remain physically moored. Before transfer, verify combined deck-and-mooring load≤6000lb. At overload or actual support destruction the cleat releases/fails and unsupported loads enter ordinary Falling; a separately valid active support retains only its actual scope. Crossing the rating is not silently forbidden after the fact.
supportStates.departure: Once the worker, case and all intended cargo are actually aboard, the airlock has completed its cycle and both operators are at stations, spend one coordinated6second event to start/hold the engine and unmoor. It consumes0.1powered minute and grants no horizontal travel in addition. The next travel leg starts after this event. If a prerequisite fails, remain moored; no free unsupported transition.
supportStates.canopy: A trained pilot at the actual station spends one Action to deploy. During a normal powered deployment, the NEW governor holds the existing position for these6seconds, consumes actual fuel and requires intact hull; the command must finish to provide canopy support. On completion the engine switches off and the fixed canopy schedule begins. This deployment is the vessel event for that round. Fuel/hull loss before completion causes an actual fall until a legal completed deployment or other support takes effect.
supportStates.falling: Without an actual valid support, start ordinary Falling using the existing marker/impact procedure. No immediate extra drop, free pause, rebased marker or automatic recovery is added by the vessel. Occupants follow the current carrier/body rules; a detached falling creature has its own actual support history.

airlock.geometry: One10x10x12ft chamber, an inner10ft door to the main cabin and an outer10ft door to the gangplank. Each door/valve can be operated from either side of that door; the outer door also has an ordinary control at the cabin service station. Each opening/closing is an Action. Both start closed; working protection is initially present when cabin air is active. Door bodies AC15HP20 each, no attacks or autonomous movement.
airlock.interlock: Opening one door normally requires the other closed. The inner door additionally requires protected airlock status. Forcing a door open or destroying it defeats that physical interlock and creates its real breach; it does not magically preserve cabin protection.
airlock.outsideCycle: Open inner, move using actual legal movement into airlock, close inner, open outer, move to the gangplank/deck, then close outer. Actions and movement may share a normal6second interval only when the actor has those actual budgets and sufficient Speed. Main cabin stays protected while inner remains closed. The airlock becomes unprotected when outer opens; people beyond it are exposed according to actual protection.
airlock.purge: When both intact doors are closed and the hull seal and running cartridge work, begin60uninterrupted elapsed seconds to restore airlock protection. Opening a door restarts an unfinished purge. These are machinery/observation seconds, not Transition work. Protection begins on completion before a same-instant exposure or hood-expiry evaluation. Closing a door does not repair a hull breach or regenerate the cartridge.
airlock.returnCycle: Open outer, move physically into airlock, close outer, wait the actual60second purge, open inner and move into cabin, then close inner. Bodies must fit fully; no entry through occupied cells or solids. Actual no-breath/other protective abilities retain their printed scope. If the inner door is forced open while the chamber is unsafe, cabin protection is lost until both doors are repaired/closed, hull breaches patched and an actual60second purge completes. Air charge continues throughout.
airlock.protectionBoundary: At a completed safe closure/purge or existing-source protection expiration use the actual timestamp. An unprotected minute accumulated before protection is restored still produces its due save; the restoration prevents only later exposure. A hazard event exactly at restoration is avoided under the explicit completion-first order. A hood expiring during purge leaves its wearer exposed until protection really returns.
